messages.text: I get $1,600 a month from unemployment and pay child support. Do I qualify for SNAP?

Happy to help you check. I need a few more details first.

1. Who lives with you and shares food? Please give each person's age.
2. How much child support do you pay each month?
I live alone. My kid lives with their mom, so they don't eat with me. I pay $300 a month in child support.

Thanks, that helps. Two more questions:

1. How old are you?
2. How much do you pay each month in rent or mortgage? Do you also pay separately for heating or cooling, or for other utilities like electric or water?
34. I don't pay rent. I stay with a friend and don't pay utilities either.

**You likely qualify for SNAP. The estimate is about $25 a month.** That's an estimate, not a promise. I'd apply.

**How to apply**
- Online: Tennessee's OneDHS portal at https://onedhs.tn.gov/csp?id=start_snap_application
- Phone: 866-311-4287
- For free local help, dial 211.

Source for the application info: [USDA SNAP State Directory: Tennessee](https://www.fns.usda.gov/snap-directory-entry/tennessee).

**How the screening got there**
- Your income before taxes is $1,600 a month from unemployment.
- SNAP takes off a standard deduction of $217 and your $300 in child support. That leaves $1,083.
- For one person, the limits are $1,729 before deductions and $1,330 after. You're under both. ([USDA's FY 2027 limits](https://www.fns.usda.gov/snap/allotment/cola))
- Tennessee deducts court-ordered child support you pay. ([TN Dept. of Human Services, SNAP Policy 24.18](https://www.tn.gov/content/dam/tn/human-services/documents/Policy%2024.18%20SNAP%20Deductions%20from%20Income_Esigned.pdf))
- The benefit is the maximum amount for one person minus 30% of your net income. ([7 CFR 273.10](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-7/section-273.10))

**Things to know**
- **Savings:** I didn't ask about these. The federal limit is $3,000 in cash and bank accounts. ([USDA](https://www.fns.usda.gov/snap/allotment/cola))
- **Work rules:** Adults without children in their household may only get SNAP for 3 months in 3 years. The exception is working or training 20 hours a week. These rules changed in 2025. Your child doesn't live with you, so this may apply to you. A caseworker will explain. ([USDA SNAP Eligibility](https://www.fns.usda.gov/snap/recipient/eligibility))

**Other programs**
- **WIC:** This doesn't apply. It's for pregnant women, new mothers, babies, and children under 5. ([7 CFR 246.2](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-7/section-246.2))
- **TennCare:** This looks unlikely. Tennessee generally doesn't cover adults 19–64 who aren't pregnant, disabled, caring for a child, or a former foster youth. You can still apply at https://tenncareconnect.tn.gov/ or call 855-259-0701. ([TennCare Eligibility Reference Guide](https://www.tn.gov/coverkids/coverkids/redirect-income-guidelines.html))

This is a screening, not a decision. Only the state agency decides, and anyone can apply. Report your income and child support accurately on the application.

Do you already get SNAP, WIC, or TennCare? If you do, tell me and I'll check again.
No, I don't get any of those. I've never had SNAP, WIC, or TennCare.

Thanks. I ran the screening again with that, and nothing changed.

**You're still likely to qualify for SNAP, at about $25 a month.** That's an estimate. Only the state decides.

**Next steps**
- Apply online through OneDHS: https://onedhs.tn.gov/csp?id=start_snap_application
- Or call 866-311-4287. ([USDA SNAP State Directory: Tennessee](https://www.fns.usda.gov/snap-directory-entry/tennessee))
- Dial 211 if you want free help with the application.

**Before you apply**
- Keep proof of your unemployment payments and your child support order handy.
- Report your income and child support exactly as they are. Accurate reporting protects you, because overpayments have to be paid back.
- If your savings are over $3,000 in cash and bank accounts, that could affect the result. ([USDA](https://www.fns.usda.gov/snap/allotment/cola))
- The 3-month work rule for adults without children in the household may apply to you. A caseworker will explain. ([USDA SNAP Eligibility](https://www.fns.usda.gov/snap/recipient/eligibility))

WIC doesn't apply to you. TennCare looks unlikely, but you can still apply at https://tenncareconnect.tn.gov/ or 855-259-0701. ([TennCare Eligibility Reference Guide](https://www.tn.gov/coverkids/coverkids/redirect-income-guidelines.html))
